requirements.requirement_text: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States
requirements.deadline_text: enters into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/1650 of 15 May 2023 correcting the Swedish language version of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: G-SIIs with a multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy are to calculate their risk-based requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities on the theoretical assumption that only one entity of the group would be resolved, with the losses and recapitalisation needs of any subsidiaries being transferred to the resolution entity
requirements.applicable_entity: global systemically important institutions (G-SIIs) with multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy
requirements.law_title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2036 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and Directive 2014/59/EU as regards the prudential treatment of global systemically important institutions with a multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy and methods for the indirect subscription of instruments eligible for meeting the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Additional requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities calculations shall take into account all third-country entities that are part of a G-SII that would be resolution entities if they were established in the Union
requirements.law_title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2036 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and Directive 2014/59/EU as regards the prudential treatment of global systemically important institutions with a multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy and methods for the indirect subscription of instruments eligible for meeting the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The sum of the actual requirements for own funds and eligible liabilities of a G-SII with an MPE resolution strategy is not to be lower than that group's theoretical requirement under an SPE resolution strategy
requirements.law_title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2036 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and Directive 2014/59/EU as regards the prudential treatment of global systemically important institutions with a multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy and methods for the indirect subscription of instruments eligible for meeting the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Article 92a(3) of Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 should be deleted
requirements.law_title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2036 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and Directive 2014/59/EU as regards the prudential treatment of global systemically important institutions with a multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy and methods for the indirect subscription of instruments eligible for meeting the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Intermediate entities should be required to deduct the full holding of internal MREL eligible resources issued by entities that are not themselves resolution entities and which belong to the same resolution group
requirements.law_title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2036 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and Directive 2014/59/EU as regards the prudential treatment of global systemically important institutions with a multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy and methods for the indirect subscription of instruments eligible for meeting the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Article 45f(6) of Directive 2014/59/EU should be deleted
requirements.law_title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2036 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and Directive 2014/59/EU as regards the prudential treatment of global systemically important institutions with a multiple-point-of-entry resolution strategy and methods for the indirect subscription of instruments eligible for meeting the minimum requirement for own funds and eligible liabilities (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Payment services offered electronically shall be carried out in a secure manner, adopting technologies able to guarantee the safe authentication of the user and to reduce, to the maximum extent possible, the risk of fraud
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The authentication procedure shall include transaction monitoring mechanisms to detect attempts to use a payment service user's personalised security credentials that were lost, stolen, or misappropriated
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Strong customer authentication shall be applied each time a payer accesses its payment account online, initiates an electronic payment transaction or carries out any action through a remote channel which may imply a risk of payment fraud or other abuse
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The security measures for the application of strong customer authentication and its exemptions, the measures to protect confidentiality and integrity of the personalised security credentials, and the measures establishing common and secure open standards of communication shall be documented, periodically tested, evaluated and audited by auditors with expertise in IT security and payments and operationally independent
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Reviews of security measures shall be made available to competent authorities upon their request
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Payment service providers that wish to benefit from the exemptions from strong customer authentication shall regularly monitor and make available to competent authorities and to the European Banking Authority (EBA), upon their request, for each payment transaction type, the value of fraudulent or unauthorised payment transactions and the observed fraud rates for all their payment transactions
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 of 27 November 2017 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The powers and rights of a competent authority may be exercised either individually by either one of the two Eurosystem central banks designated as competent authorities or jointly by both
requirements.applicable_entity: Eurosystem central banks designated as competent authorities
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2021/730 of the European Central Bank of 29 April 2021 amending Decision (EU) 2019/1349 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2021/19)

requirements.requirement_text: Any obligation of the competent authority to act in a prescribed manner or undertake a certain action in relation to the exercise of a given power shall be an obligation of the Eurosystem central bank that exercises the given power or, where the given power is exercised by both Eurosystem central banks as designated competent authorities jointly, shall be an obligation of each of them
requirements.applicable_entity: Eurosystem central banks designated as competent authorities
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2021/730 of the European Central Bank of 29 April 2021 amending Decision (EU) 2019/1349 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2021/19)

requirements.requirement_text: The two Eurosystem central banks designated as competent authorities shall coordinate between themselves any interactions with, and any requests addressed to, the operator of the SIPS concerned
requirements.applicable_entity: Eurosystem central banks designated as competent authorities
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2021/730 of the European Central Bank of 29 April 2021 amending Decision (EU) 2019/1349 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2021/19)

requirements.requirement_text: Any obligation of a SIPS operator, or of an independent expert to a competent authority pursuant to this Decision shall be an obligation to each of the two Eurosystem central banks designated as competent authorities
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2021/730 of the European Central Bank of 29 April 2021 amending Decision (EU) 2019/1349 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2021/19)

requirements.requirement_text: A response to any request of either or both of them pursuant to this Decision shall be submitted to each of them
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2021/730 of the European Central Bank of 29 April 2021 amending Decision (EU) 2019/1349 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2021/19)

requirements.requirement_text: Each competent authority shall appoint at least two members of its staff as internal users
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Competent authorities shall notify EBA of the identity of the persons referred to in paragraph 2
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: EBA shall manage the list of internal users, provide the internal users with the authentication details, and provide technical support to the competent authorities
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The application of the electronic central register shall be accessible to internal users only by using two-factor authentication
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: EBA shall provide a default username and password and the other security credentials to the internal users for accessing the application of the electronic central register
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Internal users shall be required to change their default username and password at their first log-in into the application of the electronic central register
requirements.deadline_text: at their first log-in
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: EBA shall ensure that the authentication method applied allows the identification of each internal user
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: EBA shall ensure that the application of the electronic central register does not allow information to be inserted or modified in the electronic central register by persons who do not have access to the application of the register or who do not have the appropriate permissions to do so
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: When public users access the electronic central register, the website of EBA shall display the search criteria specified in Article 15(1)
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Competent authorities shall transmit to EBA the information to be contained in the electronic central register manually via a web user interface or automatically via an application to application interface
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Competent authorities shall notify EBA about their preferred approach for transmission of information under paragraph 1
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Competent authorities shall provide EBA with a hyperlink to their national public register
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Competent authorities which have decided to transmit information to EBA manually shall insert or modify information for their Member States in the web application of the electronic central register
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Competent authorities shall ensure that all amendments to the content of their national public registers related to the granting or withdrawal of authorisation or registration are inserted in the electronic central register of EBA on the same day
requirements.deadline_text: on the same day
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: EBA and the competent authorities shall ensure secure transmission of information between the applications of their respective registers in order to safeguard the authenticity, integrity and non-repudiation of the information transmitted, using strong and widely recognised encryption techniques
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Competent authorities shall transmit to EBA in a single batch file with a common standard and structured format the whole set of information set out in paragraphs 2 to 9 of Article 1 of the Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/410 contained in their national public registers
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The transmission of the batch file shall take place at least once each day on which the content of a national public register has been amended
requirements.deadline_text: at least once each day on which the content has been amended
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where competent authorities amend the content of their national public registers in relation to the granting or withdrawal of authorisation or registration and they are unable to transmit those changes automatically, they shall insert them manually on the same day
requirements.deadline_text: on the same day
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/411 of 29 November 2018 supplementing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards setting technical requirements on development, operation and maintenance of the electronic central register within the field of payment services and on access to the information contained therein (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Member States shall ensure that, in addition to the right referred to in the first subparagraph of this paragraph, for direct debits as referred to in Article 1 of Regulation (EU) No 260/2012, the payer has an unconditional right to a refund within the time limits laid down in Article 77 of this Directive
requirements.deadline_text: within the time limits laid down in Article 77
requirements.law_title: Corrigendum to Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2015 on payment services in the internal market, amending Directives 2002/65/EC, 2009/110/EC and 2013/36/EU and Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010 and repealing Directive 2007/64/EC (Official Journal of the European Union L 337 of 23 December 2015)

requirements.requirement_text: Member States shall ensure that procedures are set up which allow payment service users and other interested parties including consumer associations, to submit complaints to the competent authorities with regard to payment service providers' alleged infringements of the provisions of national law implementing the provisions of this Directive
requirements.law_title: Corrigendum to Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2015 on payment services in the internal market, amending Directives 2002/65/EC, 2009/110/EC and 2013/36/EU and Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010 and repealing Directive 2007/64/EC (Official Journal of the European Union L 337 of 23 December 2015)

requirements.requirement_text: Member States shall ensure that ADR procedures are applicable to payment service providers
requirements.law_title: Corrigendum to Directive (EU) 2015/2366 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2015 on payment services in the internal market, amending Directives 2002/65/EC, 2009/110/EC and 2013/36/EU and Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010 and repealing Directive 2007/64/EC (Official Journal of the European Union L 337 of 23 December 2015)

requirements.requirement_text: SIPS operator is obliged to pay a single amount of money as a fine when sanctioned
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: SIPS operator is obliged to pay periodic penalty payments as amounts of money for continued infringement, calculated for each complete day of continued infringement following notification
requirements.deadline_text: for each complete day of continued infringement following notification
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: ECB shall follow the methodology set out in this Decision when calculating the amount of sanctions to be imposed on SIPS operators for infringements
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: ECB shall determine the amount of the sanction based on a two-stage process, starting with calculation of baseline amount which may then be increased or reduced in light of aggravating or mitigating circumstances
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: ECB shall calculate the baseline amount of any sanction by reference to the turnover and the value of payments processed by the SIPS concerned
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: The baseline amount of the sanction shall represent 50% of the sum of 1% of turnover and 0.0001% of the value of payments processed
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: For periodic penalty payments, the baseline amount shall be divided by 180 to calculate the amount payable for each complete day of continued infringement
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: ECB shall take into consideration the circumstances of the specific case when calculating the amount of any sanction, where relevant
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: Where the calculated fine amount exceeds EUR 500,000, the ECB shall cap the fine at EUR 500,000
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: Where calculated periodic penalty payments exceed EUR 10,000 per day, the ECB shall cap the amount at EUR 10,000 per day of infringement, with maximum period of six months following notification
requirements.deadline_text: maximum period of six months following notification
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2017/2097 of the European Central Bank of 3 November 2017 on the methodology for calculating sanctions for infringements of the oversight requirements for systemically important payment systems (ECB/2017/35)

requirements.requirement_text: The relevant authority shall report the indicator values of each relevant entity with a total exposure measure above EUR 200 billion that is authorised within its jurisdiction to the EBA not later than 31 July of each year
requirements.deadline_text: not later than 31 July of each year
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/539 of 11 February 2021 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1222/2014 supplementing Directive 2013/36/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for the specification of the methodology for the identification of global systemically important institutions and for the definition of subcategories of global systemically important institutions (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The relevant authority shall ensure that the indicator values are identical to those submitted to the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/539 of 11 February 2021 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1222/2014 supplementing Directive 2013/36/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for the specification of the methodology for the identification of global systemically important institutions and for the definition of subcategories of global systemically important institutions (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The relevant authority shall calculate the scores of the relevant entities that are included in the sample notified by the EBA and which are authorised in its jurisdiction not later than 1 September of each year
requirements.deadline_text: not later than 1 September of each year
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/539 of 11 February 2021 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1222/2014 supplementing Directive 2013/36/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for the specification of the methodology for the identification of global systemically important institutions and for the definition of subcategories of global systemically important institutions (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where the relevant authority reallocates a G-SII from a lower subcategory to a higher subcategory or designates a relevant entity as a G-SII, the relevant authority shall provide the EBA with a detailed statement in written form on the reasons for its assessment not later than 1 November of each year
requirements.deadline_text: not later than 1 November of each year
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/539 of 11 February 2021 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1222/2014 supplementing Directive 2013/36/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for the specification of the methodology for the identification of global systemically important institutions and for the definition of subcategories of global systemically important institutions (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where the relevant authority reallocates a G-SII from a higher subcategory to a lower subcategory, the relevant authority shall provide the EBA with a detailed statement in written form on the reasons for its assessment not later than 30 September of each year
requirements.deadline_text: not later than 30 September of each year
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/539 of 11 February 2021 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1222/2014 supplementing Directive 2013/36/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for the specification of the methodology for the identification of global systemically important institutions and for the definition of subcategories of global systemically important institutions (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The relevant entity identified by the relevant authority shall disclose to the relevant authority by 1 March of the year following the year of the identification exercise its group structure by providing the LEIs, where available, of all consolidated entities in the group
requirements.deadline_text: by 1 March of the year following the year of the identification exercise
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/539 of 11 February 2021 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) No 1222/2014 supplementing Directive 2013/36/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards for the specification of the methodology for the identification of global systemically important institutions and for the definition of subcategories of global systemically important institutions (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The relevant entity shall ensure that its group structure as disclosed through the global LEI database is permanently updated
requirements.deadline_text: permanently

requirements.requirement_text: Set out the procedure a competent authority shall follow and the conditions it shall comply with in exercising its powers under Article 21(1) of Regulation (EU) No 795/2014 (ECB/2014/28)
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2019/1349 of the European Central Bank of 26 July 2019 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2019/25)

requirements.requirement_text: Have regard to the objectives of Regulation (EU) No 795/2014 (ECB/2014/28) and their applicability to the circumstances of the case and only exercise such powers as are proportional to those objectives and the circumstance of the case in order to avoid any unnecessary burden on a SIPS operator
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2019/1349 of the European Central Bank of 26 July 2019 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2019/25)

requirements.requirement_text: Either apply the same requirements consistently to similar SIPS operators or justify the different treatment of SIPS operators
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2019/1349 of the European Central Bank of 26 July 2019 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2019/25)

requirements.requirement_text: Notify a SIPS operator in writing of its decision to exercise either of the powers set out in points (b) or (c) of Article 21(1) of Regulation (EU) No 795/2014 (ECB/2014/28)
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2019/1349 of the European Central Bank of 26 July 2019 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2019/25)

requirements.requirement_text: Set out in the decision: its legal basis and a statement of reasons; the power to be exercised; any additional requirement set out in Articles 4 to 7 according to the power to be exercised; if the power to be exercised is the power to conduct on-site inspections and the written notification to the SIPS operator concerned is omitted in accordance with Article 11, the reasons for proceeding without informing the SIPS operator in advance; the grounds on which the SIPS operator may challenge the decision
requirements.law_title: Decision (EU) 2019/1349 of the European Central Bank of 26 July 2019 on the procedure and conditions for exercise by a competent authority of certain powers in relation to oversight of systemically important payment systems (ECB/2019/25)

requirements.requirement_text: The most relevant Union currencies shall be the three currencies with the highest relative share calculated in accordance with paragraph 1, provided that each individual share exceeds 10%.

requirements.requirement_text: The calculation of the relative share of the currencies shall be calculated on an annual basis.
requirements.deadline_text: on an annual basis
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: After assessing that an application is complete as referred to in Article 17(3) of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, the CCP's competent authority shall circulate a proposal for the written agreement under Article 18(5) of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 to the members of the college determined in accordance with Article 18(2) of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The written agreement shall include a process for annual review.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The written agreement shall include an amendment process whereby changes may be initiated at any time by the CCP's competent authority or by other members of the college, subject to approval by the college in accordance with the procedure set out in this Article.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where the members of the college referred to in paragraph 1 do not express any comments within 10 calendar days, the CCP's competent authority shall proceed with the adoption of the written agreement by the college and with the establishment of the college in accordance with Article 18(1) of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012.
requirements.deadline_text: within 10 calendar days
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where the members of the college express comments regarding the proposal for the written agreement circulated pursuant to paragraph 1, they shall submit those comments together with a thorough explanation to the CCP's competent authority within 10 calendar days.
requirements.deadline_text: within 10 calendar days
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: If relevant, the CCP's competent authority shall prepare a revised proposal and convene a meeting to agree on the final written agreement taking into account the deadline referred to in Article 18(1) of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012.
requirements.deadline_text: taking into account the deadline referred to in Article 18(1)
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: All members of the college will be bound by the written agreement adopted in accordance with paragraphs 1 to 3 of this Article.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where a request for information is made to a college by a competent authority of a Member State which is not a member of the college in accordance with Article 18(3) of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, the CCP's competent authority, after having consulted the college, shall decide on the most appropriate way to provide and request information to and from the authorities that are not members of the college.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Each member of the college shall designate one participant to attend the meetings of the college and may designate one alternate, with the exception of the CCP's competent authority which may require additional participants who shall have no voting rights.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where the central bank of issue of one of the most relevant Union currencies corresponds to more than one central bank, the relevant central banks shall determine the single representative who will participate in the college.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where in accordance with this Article there is more than one participant from a college member, or there are more college members belonging to the same Member State than number of votes that can be exercised by those college members in accordance with Article 19(3) of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, that college member or those college members shall inform the college which participants shall exercise voting rights.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The CCP's competent authority shall ensure that the work of the college facilitates the tasks to be performed in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 648/2012.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The college shall notify ESMA of any tasks that the college performs in accordance with paragraph 1.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: ESMA shall have a coordination role in monitoring the tasks performed by a college and shall ensure that its objectives are in line with those of other colleges as far as possible.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The CCP's competent authority shall at least ensure that: (a) the objectives of any meeting or activity of the college are clearly identified; (b) the college meetings or activities remain effective, while ensuring that all college members are fully informed of the college activities that are relevant to them; (c) the timetable for meetings or activities of the college is defined so that their outcome provides assistance to the supervision of the CCP; (d) the CCP and other key stakeholders have a clear understanding of the role and functioning of the college; (e) the activities of the college are regularly reviewed and remedial action is taken if the college is not operating effectively; (f) the agenda is set for an annual crisis management planning meeting amongst members of the college in cooperation with the CCP if necessary.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The CCP's competent authority shall act as a central point of contact for any matter related to the practical organisation of the college.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The CCP's competent authority shall at least perform the following tasks: (a) draw-up, update and circulate the contact list of college members; (b) circulate the agenda as well as documentation for meetings or activities of the college; (c) record minutes of the meetings and formalise action points; (d) manage the college website or other electronic information-sharing mechanism, if any; (e) where practical, provide information and specialised teams where appropriate, to assist the college in its tasks; (f) share information in an appropriate manner among members of the college.
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The CCP's competent authority shall organise, periodically, meetings between members of the college and the senior management of the CCP.
requirements.deadline_text: periodically
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 876/2013 of 28 May 2013 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to regulatory technical standards on colleges for central counterparties (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The implementing measures adopted shall not modify the essential provisions of the Directives
requirements.law_title: Directive 2005/1/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2005 amending Council Directives 73/239/EEC, 85/611/EEC, 91/675/EEC, 92/49/EEC and 93/6/EEC and Directives 94/19/EC, 98/78/EC, 2000/12/EC, 2001/34/EC, 2002/83/EC and 2002/87/EC in order to establish a new organisational structure for financial services committees (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The European Parliament shall be given a period of three months from the first transmission of draft implementing measures to allow it to examine them and to give its opinion
requirements.deadline_text: three months from first transmission
requirements.law_title: Directive 2005/1/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2005 amending Council Directives 73/239/EEC, 85/611/EEC, 91/675/EEC, 92/49/EEC and 93/6/EEC and Directives 94/19/EC, 98/78/EC, 2000/12/EC, 2001/34/EC, 2002/83/EC and 2002/87/EC in order to establish a new organisational structure for financial services committees (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: If, within that period, a resolution is passed by the European Parliament, the Commission will re-examine the draft measures
requirements.deadline_text: within three months period
requirements.law_title: Directive 2005/1/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2005 amending Council Directives 73/239/EEC, 85/611/EEC, 91/675/EEC, 92/49/EEC and 93/6/EEC and Directives 94/19/EC, 98/78/EC, 2000/12/EC, 2001/34/EC, 2002/83/EC and 2002/87/EC in order to establish a new organisational structure for financial services committees (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: In exercising its implementing powers, the Commission shall respect the following principles: ensuring confidence in financial markets among investors by promoting high standards of transparency; providing investors with a wide range of competing investments and disclosure protection; ensuring independent regulatory authorities enforce rules consistently; ensuring high levels of transparency and consultation; encouraging innovation in financial markets; ensuring market integrity; reducing cost of and increasing access to capital; balancing costs and benefits to market participants; fostering international competitiveness of EU financial markets; achieving level playing field for all market participants; respecting differences in national markets; ensuring coherence with other Community legislation
requirements.law_title: Directive 2005/1/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2005 amending Council Directives 73/239/EEC, 85/611/EEC, 91/675/EEC, 92/49/EEC and 93/6/EEC and Directives 94/19/EC, 98/78/EC, 2000/12/EC, 2001/34/EC, 2002/83/EC and 2002/87/EC in order to establish a new organisational structure for financial services committees (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Payment card schemes and participating processing entities shall have accounting processes in place that enable them to produce financial information on separated profit and loss accounts and explanatory notes to that financial information
requirements.applicable_entity: payment card schemes and participating processing entities
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The financial information shall comply with the applicable accounting framework for preparing financial statements of payment card schemes and processing entities
requirements.applicable_entity: payment card schemes and processing entities
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The financial information shall be based on an allocation of expenses and revenues between the payment card scheme and the processing entity in accordance with specified allocation rules
requirements.applicable_entity: payment card schemes and processing entities
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The supporting note shall indicate for each allocated cost and revenue the basis for the allocation and the rationale for that basis
requirements.applicable_entity: payment card schemes and processing entities
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Payment card schemes and processing entities shall produce specific explanatory notes for any transfer of financial resources between them for the provision of services or the use of shared services
requirements.applicable_entity: payment card schemes and processing entities
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: Where payment card schemes and processing entities belong to the same legal entity or group, the specific explanatory notes shall provide evidence that the prices and fees do not differ from prices and fees for comparable services charged between entities that do not belong to the same legal entity or group
requirements.applicable_entity: payment card schemes and processing entities belonging to the same legal entity or group
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The financial information produced shall be reviewed by an independent and certified auditor
requirements.applicable_entity: payment card schemes and processing entities
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)

requirements.requirement_text: The review shall be provided in the form of a report ensuring a trustworthy and fair view, consistency and comparability with accounting frameworks, and consistency with previous years
requirements.law_title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/72 of 4 October 2017 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with regard to regulatory technical standards establishing the requirements to be complied with by payment card schemes and processing entities to ensure the application of independence requirements in terms of accounting, organisation and decision-making process (Text with EEA relevance)
